diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose that the initial state $u_0$ follows a (nonzero mean) Gaussian distribution with the identity covariance, i.e., $u_0 \sim \mathcal{N}(m, \mathbf{I})$
Hence, the parameterization~\eqref{eqn:cov} for $\Sigma_{\theta}$ in the Gaussian noise setting is optimal in the sense that $H_p(u_{t-1}|u_t) = H_{q_{\theta}}(u_{t-1}|u_t)$.
obtained from corrupting the output $u$ by an additive Gaussian noise $\eta \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma(a))$, i.e., $u_{\eta} = u + \eta$.
The model is trained on the noisy data set with $\sigma=0.0005$.

issues.failure_explanation: The covariance $\beta_t\mathbf{I}$ for the reverse kernel is derived (Appendix C.3) only under $u_0\sim\mathcal N(m,\mathbf I)$: then $\mathrm{Cov}(u_t)=\mathbf I$ for all $t$ and the true reverse covariance is $\beta_t\mathbf I$. The paper's Gaussian-noise setting is $u_0|a\sim\mathcal N(u,\sigma^2\mathbf I)$ with $\sigma\ll 1$ (0.0005, 0.001, 1%, 5%), or general $\Sigma(a)$. For $u_0\sim\mathcal N(m,\sigma^2\mathbf I)$ the true reverse covariance is $\beta_t v_{t-1}/(\alpha_t v_{t-1}+\beta_t)\,\mathbf I$ with $v_{t-1}=\bar\alpha_{t-1}\sigma^2+1-\bar\alpha_{t-1}$, which for small $\sigma$ is close to $\tilde\beta_t=\frac{1-\bar\alpha_{t-1}}{1-\bar\alpha_t}\beta_t$, not $\beta_t$. So prop:added-2 is applied outside its hypothesis, and the asserted optimality ($H_p(u_{t-1}|u_t)=H_{q_\theta}(u_{t-1}|u_t)$) of the $\beta_t\mathbf I$ choice fails in the regime actually used.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restrict the Gaussian-noise case of eqn:cov and the optimality statement to unit-covariance noise, or derive and use the $\sigma$-dependent (or $\Sigma(a)$-dependent) conditional covariance of the true reverse kernel, presenting the current choice as a heuristic otherwise.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical rationale for the case split in eqn:cov and the optimality claim for the Gaussian-noise covariance are unsupported for the noise models the paper considers; the reverse sampler's variance in the noisy experiments is not the one matching the true reverse process.
issues.title: Reverse covariance beta_t I prescribed for all additive Gaussian noise but justified only for identity noise covariance
issues.why_classification: A contained new computation (correct reverse covariance for general Gaussian noise) or an explicit weakening of scope is needed; the optimality claim for the advertised noisy regime is lost, but no global architecture changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \# of samples $N_s$   &  $1$ if noise-free; $500$ if noisy

issues.failure_explanation: MSTD is defined as the norm of the sample standard deviation of $N_s$ samples divided by $N_s$. The hyper-parameter tables for the noise-free experiments (Tests 2, 3, 4) state $N_s=1$, for which the sample standard deviation is undefined (or identically zero), so the metric cannot produce the nonzero MSTD values reported in Tables tab:darcy_error, tab:burgers, tab:adv_error. Additionally, dividing a standard deviation by the number of samples $N_s$ has no statistical meaning (it is not a standard error nor a relative quantity), so the reported MSTD numbers are not interpretable as the 'uncertainty' quantity the text claims.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the actual number of samples used for the MSTD diagnostic and fix the definition (e.g. normalize by $\|u\|_2$ or report the raw norm), consistent with the reported numbers.
issues.overall_effect: The reported MSTD values and the accompanying claims about learned uncertainty in the noise-free tables are not reproducible from the stated definition and protocol.
issues.title: MSTD metric is ill-defined under the stated protocol ($N_s=1$) yet nonzero values are reported
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the metric definition and experimental protocol description suffices; no theoretical claim depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
H_{q_{\theta}}(u_T) + \sum_{t=1}^T H_{q_{\theta}}(u_{t-1} | u_t) 
=
H_p(u_T) + \sum_{t=1}^T H_p(u_{t-1} | u_t)
where $\epsilon_{\theta}(t, u_t, a)$ is a neural network function that approximates the the standard Gaussian $\epsilon_t$.

issues.failure_explanation: The display only shows $\mathbb E_{q_\theta}[-\log q_\theta]=\mathbb E_p[-\log p]$, i.e. equality of the entropies of two Gaussian chains with matching covariances. Entropy of a Gaussian depends only on covariance, so this holds regardless of the learned means $m_\theta$ and says nothing about the likelihood of $p$-data under $q_\theta$ ($\mathbb E_p[-\log q_\theta]$, the cross-entropy), which is what 'exact likelihood under the true model' would mean. Matching entropies does not imply $q_\theta=p$; the claim is unsupported (and false whenever $\epsilon_\theta\neq\epsilon_t$).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the sentence with the accurate statement that the chosen covariances match the differential entropies of the true reverse kernels (under the respective hypotheses), without claiming exact likelihood.
issues.overall_effect: The concluding optimality/exactness claim of Appendix C.3 overstates what the two propositions establish; the covariance choice is justified only as matching the conditional entropy, not the likelihood.
issues.title: Equality of entropies misrepresented as achieving exact likelihood under the true model
issues.why_classification: Withdrawing the misstatement is a local edit; no other result relies on it.
